note: Exercise compr-is-kernel (eff.tex:4020): f is a comprehension for p iff f is a kernel of p^perp. Stated as an iff, both directions as in bsols.tex:2832.

Definition (eff.tex:4031): f is pure if f = pi after xi for some comprehension pi and quotient xi. The existentials bind the intermediate object, both maps and both predicates, which is the intended reading. The purity discussion 201III-201V is not formalized and carries no DISP.

Definition (eff.tex:4080) clause 1: im f is the LEAST predicate on Y with (im f) after f = 1 after f, and C has images when every map has one. Both the defining equation and the minimality are stated. The clause's closing Note - that im^perp f is the GREATEST predicate with (im^perp f) after f = 0 - is not rendered as a statement anywhere (it is an immediate dualization and is used implicitly inside 203IV.5 and 205IV).

Definition (eff.tex:4097) clause 2: f is faithful if im f = 1, equivalently p after f = 0 implies p = 0. Both the definition and the "that is" reformulation are rendered, the latter proved (the thesis asserts the equivalence inside a Definition without proof, so there is nothing to match).

Notation (eff.tex:4105): "im f after g is read as im (f after g)". This is a parsing convention about the printed notation, so nothing is left to formalize beyond the operator itself; the doc comment attaches the label to imPred, which is really the operator of 202I.1. Harmless label reuse, noted for the record.

Exercise im-ineq (eff.tex:4130). Both halves are rendered - im (f after g) <= im f, and the "conclude" tail im (f after alpha) = im f for any iso alpha - as the two conjuncts of one theorem. Proof is bsols.tex:2855.
Exercise exc-quot-faithful (eff.tex:4135): any quotient is faithful. Proof is bsols' (epicity of quotients).

Lemma compr-total (eff.tex:4145): in an effectus with quotients, comprehensions are total. [HasQuotients C] is assumed, as the thesis assumes. Proof follows the thesis: quotient xi for (1 after pi)^perp, total pi_t with pi = pi_t after xi, 1 after pi_t = p after pi_t by epicity, f with pi_t = pi after f, id = f after xi by monicity of pi, and finally 1 <= 1 after xi = 1 after pi.

Definition (eff.tex:4168) clause 1: p is (image) sharp if p = im f for some map f; SPred X is the set of sharp predicates on X. Matches. The Beware 203II (effintro's weaker p meet p^perp = 0 notion) and the Example 203III (sharp = projections in vN^op) are not statements of this point.

Definition (eff.tex:4177) clause 2: floor p = im pi_p and ceil p = (floor (p^perp))^perp. The parenthetical justification (comprehensions for the same predicate have the same image, by 202V) is discharged by using the chosen comprMap p.
Lemma floor-basics clause 1: floor p <= p. Proof is Ad 1 of the thesis.
Lemma floor-basics clause 2: pi_p = pi_{floor p} after alpha for some iso alpha. Proof is Ad 2: show pi_p is also a comprehension for floor p, then apply 199VII.2.
Lemma floor-basics clause 3: floor (floor p) = floor p. Proof is Ad 3 (previous clause plus 202V).
Lemma floor-basics clause 4: p <= q implies floor p <= floor q. Proof is Ad 4.
Lemma floor-basics clause 5: (ceil p) after f <= ceil (p after f). Proof reproduces Ad 5, including the factorization of f after pi_{(p after f)^perp} through pi_{p^perp} and the appeal to clause 2.
Lemma floor-basics clause 6: (ceil p) after f = 0 iff p after f = 0. Proof is Ad 6, with the supporting facts floor 1 = 1 and ceil 0 = 0 (via id being a comprehension for 1) proved as helpers.
Exercise img-of-compr (eff.tex:4284). Both halves rendered as the two conjuncts of one theorem: p is sharp iff floor p = p, and the "conclude" tail im pi_s = s for sharp s. Proof is bsols.tex:2869.
Exercise ceiling-within-ceiling (eff.tex:4289): ceil((ceil p) after f) = ceil(p after f). Proof is bsols' antisymmetry argument from monotonicity, idempotence and 203IV.5.

Exercise img-tupling (eff.tex:4295). Both halves rendered, in two theorems: im pair(f,g) = [im f, im g], and the "conclude" tail that [p,q] is sharp iff p and q are. The cancellation step of bsols.tex:2892 is isolated as the helper eq_of_ovee_eq_of_le, which the doc comment cites by line.

Lemma compr-is-full (eff.tex:4304): for sharp s, t on the same object, s <= t iff pi_s = pi_t after h for some h. Stated as an iff with the existential over h; proof is the thesis's simplified one, using 203XII in both directions.

Lemma (eff.tex:4330): in an effectus with images, im [f,g] = (im f) join (im g). Rendered as PCM.IsSup for the algebraic order of the hom-PCM, i.e. a supremum among all predicates, which is what the thesis's join means here (made explicit in 204V). Proof is the thesis's two-inequality argument.
Corollary lattice-compr (eff.tex:4353). Both halves rendered: for sharp s, t the predicate im [pi_s, pi_t] is their supremum among all predicates, and it is itself sharp. Proof is 204III plus 203XII.
